# Waterfall / bridge

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Design](#design), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Contribution-to-change bridge with computed totals, connectors, and delta labels. Type `waterfall`. Aliases: `bridge`.

## Use cases

- EBIT or cash
- Change contributions
- Budget to actual walk

## Design

**Message:** What moved a number from A to B: the steps between an opening and a closing total.

**Use when:** An opening and a closing value exist and the steps add up to the change, such as an EBIT bridge, a cash walk or budget to actual.

**Not when:** The steps are shares of different wholes (column stacked100); two values only (column with a diff annotation); the steps have no business order (bar sorted by value).

### design-waterfall-closing-total

End the bridge on a total, so the reader does not have to add up the steps. Render checks this rule and returns the warning `design-waterfall-closing-total` with severity `advice`. A `fix` patch is included only when it can apply to the input as sent; otherwise follow `suggest`, for example when waterfall items come from rows.

### design-waterfall-order

Keep the steps in their business order, such as the P&L order; sort by size only when the message is a ranking. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

### design-waterfall-horizontal

Turn the bridge horizontal when the step names do not fit upright under the columns: rotated, cut or skipped names are hard to read. Render checks this rule and returns the warning `design-waterfall-horizontal` with severity `advice`. A `fix` patch is included only when it can apply to the input as sent; otherwise follow `suggest`, for example when waterfall items come from rows.

### design-waterfall-cost-direction

In a cost bridge, set items[].direction to lowerIsBetter, so a rising cost paints bad. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

### design-waterfall-few-steps

Show about eight steps or fewer; fold the small ones into one Other step at a place that keeps the business order. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

### design-waterfall-subtotals

Add a subtotal where the business reads one, such as gross profit before overheads, so a long bridge reads in parts. This rule needs the author's judgment; render does not check it.

## Chart IDs

- `waterfall.vertical`: fixture `ebit-bridge`
- `waterfall.horizontal`: fixture `segment-cascade-horizontal`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "waterfall",
  "data": {
    "items": [
      { "id": "start", "label": "Prior", "type": "total", "value": 100 },
      { "id": "growth", "label": "Growth", "value": 25 },
      { "id": "cost", "label": "Cost", "value": -10 },
      { "id": "end", "label": "Current", "type": "total", "value": 115 }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "unit": "$k",
    "title": "Growth offsets cost to lift revenue by $15k",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Data

A `cell` is a number, null or a value object; see [Value cell](options.md#value-cell).

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| items | array | yes | Ordered bridge items; order sets accumulation and positions. Rows: label,value; optional type (delta\|subtotal\|total). |
| items[].id | string | yes | Unique bridge-item identity used by connectors and annotations. |
| items[].label | string |  | Displayed bridge-item name; defaults to its id. |
| items[].type | string |  | Delta contribution by default; subtotal and total show accumulated levels. One of `'delta'`, `'subtotal'`, `'total'`. |
| items[].value | cell |  | Signed delta contribution, or an optional check value for a subtotal or total. A check value off the running sum by more than its inputs' rounding warns derived-mismatch, and the sum is drawn. A check value off by less is disclosed: the sum is drawn, the info check-value-rounded names both numbers, and a disclosure note names them where notes.show lists 'disclosure'. An opening total without a value is derived backward from the next total that has one across plain deltas, and refused otherwise. |
| items[].segments | array |  | Named signed contributions composing this item instead of a single value. |
| items[].segments[].id | string | yes | Segment identity within its waterfall item; also names connector anchors. |
| items[].segments[].label | string |  | Displayed segment name; defaults to its id. |
| items[].segments[].value | cell | yes | Signed contribution of this segment to its item. |
| items[].segments[].colorRole | string |  | Theme color role for this segment. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| items[].segments[].scenario | string |  | AC, PY, PL, FC (or ACT, BUD, FCST). Scenario controlling this segment paint convention. |
| items[].date | string |  | ISO 8601 date associated with this bridge item. |
| items[].scenario | string |  | AC, PY, PL, FC (or ACT, BUD, FCST). Scenario for this bridge item and its default segment styling. |
| items[].direction | string |  | Under 'lowerIsBetter' a rise paints bad and a fall good (options.signColor). One of `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'`. |
| items[].toBaseline | boolean |  | Start this delta at zero and reset the accumulated contribution list. A subtotal draws the sum of the deltas since the last total or baseline subtotal, from zero; the running level carries on. |
| items[].values | cell[] |  | With data.cases: one value per case, in case order, in place of value — the signed delta of each case, or a total's opening or check value. |
| connectors | array |  | Authored connections between item levels; omission uses the default sequence. |
| connectors[].from | string | yes | Source waterfall item id. |
| connectors[].to | string | yes | Destination waterfall item id. |
| connectors[].anchor | string |  | Connect at the item sum or a named segment boundary. One of `'sum'` (or another value of its type). |
| connectors[].hidden | boolean |  | Hide this connector and start a new summation at the destination. |
| cases | array |  | Two or three cases of the same bridge side by side in each step (scenarios): each item gives values, one per case, and each case runs its own levels in its own colour, named in the key. Case bars draw no connectors, since a line to a case's next bar would cross the other case's bar; items take no value or segments, and data.connectors is refused. Under variant 'horizontal' each step's case bars stack in its row. |
| cases[].id | string | yes | Case identity without ':', which joins it to an item id ('<item>:<case>'); an annotation anchor names it as seriesId. |
| cases[].label | string |  | Displayed case name in the key; defaults to the id. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| legend | string \| object | `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'none'`, `'auto'` (or another value of its type) |  | Key position. Segment, case and scenario encodings keep their key because numeric bar labels do not name them. With these encodings, 'none' retains the key and reports waterfall-legend-required. A plain bridge keys its sign colours only when a lowerIsBetter step inverts them. |
| axisTitles | object |  |  | Authored primary value-axis title above the vertical plot, using column title styling. Waterfall draws no value ticks. Horizontal mode accepts this key but does not print it. |
| axisTitles.primary | string |  |  | 'Measure, unit' title of the value axis, e.g. 'Margin, %'. |
| variant | string | `'vertical'`, `'horizontal'` |  | Left out: vertical columns, turned into a horizontal bridge when the step names would rotate, shorten or drop, the horizontal bridge draws without a new finding, and the spec has no cases and no annotations. 'vertical' always keeps columns. A horizontal bridge draws no annotations: it suppresses them and warns horizontal-annotations-unsupported, so use vertical for annotations. |
| build | string | `'up'`, `'down'` | `'up'` | Build label in the accessible description; defaults to up. Item types and signed values determine accumulation in both modes. |
| signColor | boolean |  |  | Paint each plain step good or bad by sign × item direction, as column's signColor; zero is neutral. Default true unless the theme sets marks.bridge or a palette is named; false paints steps neutral. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `labels`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis.show`, `valueAxis.min`, `valueAxis.max`, `valueAxis.tickStep`, `valueAxis.includeZero`, `valueAxis.percent`, `valueAxis.log`, `valueAxis.reverse`, `valueAxis.gridlines`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `rowLabels`, `sort`, `topN`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. An arrow's ends show its span, so an arrow prints the rate alone unless period is true. shape: bracket \| arrow, default bracket. arrow draws one straight arrow over the marks with the rate in an oval on it, lifted until it clears them. Where no straight line clears the chart, the span is too short for the oval, a stack's inner layer is the anchor or the chart lays comparisons out itself, it draws the bracket and warns cagr-arrow-no-room. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  |  |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. |  |
| valueLine | Draws a reference line at an authored value or an engine-computed mean, with optional tolerance shading and attainment fill between the line and resolved actuals. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) | value: number \| 'mean', default mean. A number draws the line there; mean has the engine compute it. valueKind: 'fraction'. Multiply a numeric value and its tolerance by 100 before layout: 0.35 draws at 35%. Independent of data.valueKind. Omit it for values already in percent points; not valid with mean. label: string \| false. Name plus value; ${value} sets its position. A number already in the name is kept once. false hides it. side: left \| right, default right. Side of the plot the label sits on. tolerance: number \| { low, high }. A number shades that distance on both sides of the line; low and high shade an authored corridor. | No anchor is required. Value defaults to mean. Scoped means are line-only: seriesId and paired from/to compute a primary-axis mean and limit its stroke to those bands; other types refuse scope fields for a mean. Numeric values cannot use scope fields except as a category clip with tolerance or attainment. A secondary-axis line needs an acknowledged secondary scale and an explicit numeric value. Optional tolerance shades a value-axis band; optional attainment fills between the line and resolved actuals. |
| abs | Reads the anchored data value and places its formatted absolute value in a collision-managed label. | at | at: AnchorRef |  |  |

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 270 px; fit `fill`.
Below 270 px high, down to the compact floor of 280 × 180 px, the chart draws in compact mode; `belowMinimum: 'refuse'` refuses there instead.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
